data.body:
`gh_add_label` POSTs to `.../issues/{n}/labels` with no handling for a `needs-triage` label that doesn't yet exist in the consuming repository. GitHub's "add labels to an issue" endpoint does not auto-create missing labels — this is confirmed elsewhere in this repo: `scripts/issue_triage.py::apply_fallback` explicitly checks `load_repository_labels` and creates `needs-triage` via `POST /repos/{repo}/labels` before applying it when it's absent.

Because `run()` propagates any `StaleIssueError` out of the whole for-loop (per the existing fail-fast/retry-next-day design), a consuming repository that hasn't manually created `needs-triage` will fail on the very first qualifying issue, aborting processing of every other stale issue in that run, and this repeats on every scheduled run until someone notices and creates the label. This is a breaking behavior change for existing consumers of this shared, SHA-pinned workflow.

Fix: mirror `apply_fallback`'s create-if-missing (with concurrent-creation retry) before adding the label, or catch the specific "label not found" failure and log+skip the triage step so `needs-info` removal still proceeds and the run isn't blocked.
